title: Simulation of a halting register computation
statement: Fix a Boolean input $x$, an arithmetic register program $A$, its initial state $l_0$, an oracle, a multi-tape machine $D$, a choice of initial state for $D$ for each oracle index, and bounds $B,W\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that an $N$-step register computation from state $l$ and valuation $v$, with no answer yet, has halted with answer $b$. Assume that at every earlier step its configuration satisfies the register-program precondition for $D$ and the chosen oracle, and each register value plus one has binary length at most $W$. Then the tape machine compiled from $A$ can run from the initial tape configuration encoding $x,l,v$ and any output word $out$ to a halting configuration whose output is $out$ followed by $b$, with every work-tape head position between $-1$ and $W$ inclusive; its invariant holds at every earlier step.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle, multi-tape machine $D$, and oracle-indexed initial states for $D$
Natural number $N$, initial state $l$, register valuation $v$, output word $out$, and Boolean answer $b$
The $N$-step register computation is halted at time $N$ and its answer is $b$
At each time less than $N$, the precondition for the program, machine, and oracle holds
At each time less than $N$, every register value plus one has binary length at most $W$
